newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise, U.S. rate hike discounted.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise, U.S. rate hike discounted.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher in quiet trade late morning Monday as traders and analysts did not expect a negative impact from an anticipated rise in U.S. interest rates.
"Traders have discounted a rate hike in the U.S.," when the policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets Tuesday, said a trader at a local bank.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 5/8 to 90-7/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was up $0.15 to 126.85.
While traders said the market had discounted a rate hike, large investors were still waiting on the sidelines for concrete news on Tuesday, said another trader.
However, he added that fund managers and other investors were likely to enter the market quickly after the Federal Reserve gives word.
That positive view is largely based on the expected upgrade to Argentina's credit rating, which is anticipated to be announced within weeks.
